name: AI-made video ads and UGC for e-commerce brands
one_liner: Use Google Veo 3 to make AI-generated UGC-style short video ads for small online brands that don't want to film their own.
customer: Small online brands such as Shopify stores and skincare, supplement, fitness and coaching businesses
offer: AI-generated UGC and product videos for Facebook, Instagram Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts ads
how_it_makes_money: $100–300 per video, or a $500–1,000/month retainer for 4–8 videos
startup_cost: low: Veo 3 costs about $250/month (half price for the first 3 months)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; the transcript says people were making money within 2 days of launch
evidence: 'You could charge $100 to $300 bucks a pop... $500 to $1,000 a month for four to eight different videos' (Jzcuxz7IeR0)
Brands are 'tired of filming it themselves. It's thousands of dollars a month' (Jzcuxz7IeR0)
risks: Many people are already offering this, so prices may fall
Ad platforms may restrict or require labels on AI content
Some AI clips still look fake, and brands will reject them
Pricing is suggested by the presenter, not shown as real case revenue

name: White-label AI video for production agencies
one_liner: Make AI b-roll, product shots and full commercials that video and marketing agencies deliver to their clients under their own name.
customer: Video production companies and marketing agencies
offer: AI-generated commercials, b-roll, product shots and reel assets made without a film crew
how_it_makes_money: Per-project fees; one creator is quoting $10,000–15,000 per commercial after making a pharma-style ad with about $500 in credits
startup_cost: low: about $250/month for Veo plus credits (one example spent about $500 in credits)
time_to_first_revenue: weeks; in the Reddit example, agencies contacted the creator after one viral post
evidence: A Reddit user who makes $500,000 commercials for pharma companies made a comparable one in half a day with $500 in credits; agencies reached out and he is quoting $10–15K (Jzcuxz7IeR0)
'Most of these agencies don't want to mess with AI... You can be the AI whisperer behind the curtain' (Jzcuxz7IeR0)
risks: The case comes from someone with existing commercial experience
Agencies may learn to do it themselves
Client approvals and revisions can drag on
Legal and compliance limits apply in regulated sectors such as pharma

name: AI-agent outreach to sell websites to local businesses
one_liner: Use the ChatGPT browser agent to find local businesses without websites, research them and write personalised cold emails offering a website.
customer: Local tradespeople and clinics without a website (the examples are plumbers and dentists)
offer: A done-for-you website, found and pitched through automated, personalised outreach
how_it_makes_money: One-off website build fee, possibly plus monthly hosting/care (prices not stated)
evidence: Example task: 'finding every plumber in Nashville without a website, grabbing their contact info and writing personalized emails to sell them websites' (I24XPX0HS5c)
Example task: 'find 20 dentists in Austin... write custom cold emails... export to CSV with follow-up templates' (I24XPX0HS5c)
Weak: these are demo tasks, not reported revenue
risks: UK/EU rules on cold email (PECR/GDPR) limit B2C-style outreach
A crowded market with low prices
No pricing or close rates are given

name: Paid-poll-validated website add-on micro-SaaS
one_liner: Pay for a targeted poll of small business owners to find which website feature they would pay for, then build it without code and sell it.
offer: A no-code website feature such as appointment booking, a pricing calculator, a chatbot or a testimonials widget
startup_cost: low: poll costs plus an AI/no-code builder
evidence: Polled small business owners on 'What one website feature does your business need the most right now that you would be willing to pay for?' The options were booking, contact forms, testimonials, chatbot and pricing calculator (IHy07Ny72kA)
risks: Competes with many existing widgets
A poll answer is not the same as a payment
Getting customers needs distribution the poll doesn't provide

name: Niche hobby daily-deal shop plus content flywheel
one_liner: Build a daily-deal e-commerce site and a paid magazine for one hobby niche, fed by free YouTube tutorials.
offer: Daily-deal e-commerce, a print/digital magazine and tutorial content
how_it_makes_money: Product margin plus a $6-per-issue magazine with tens of thousands of subscribers; repurposed YouTube content brings in several million dollars a year
time_to_first_revenue: months; it took years to build the audience
evidence: '$6 per issue and tens of thousands of subscribers... several million dollars a year just repurposing my YouTube' (Kg66hxP9tzc)
Launched quiltersdailydeal.com, 'one of those [deal sites] aimed at my mom' (Kg66hxP9tzc)
'Somebody make the baking version. Somebody make the woodworking version' (Kg66hxP9tzc)
risks: Depends on a personality-led content engine that takes a long time to build
The success story is an outlier
Holding inventory adds working capital

name: Bulk liquidation and wholesale brokering to resellers
one_liner: Source surplus stock in bulk (clothes, watches, beauty products) and sell it cheaply to resellers, leaving them most of the margin.
offer: Repeatable bulk lots of discounted inventory
how_it_makes_money: A small margin on volume; for example, a shirt sold for $5 that the reseller sells for $30
startup_cost: low to medium: 'a few hundred' risked to secure a deal worth about $80K of clothes, financed through credibility
evidence: Built a watch business by contacting every eBay watch seller; one partner showed up the next day (IYotH4hI4KA)
'If you don't think it's worth risking a few hundred to buy 80 grand worth of clothes, it's not for you' (IYotH4hI4KA)
Health and beauty: products bought for about $100 sell for $500 (IYotH4hI4KA)
risks: Needs supplier access and trust
Counterfeit and scam reputation risk
Logistics and capital tied up in stock

name: College-town couch flipping
one_liner: Buy used couches cheaply in college towns and resell them, with delivery, at the start of each term.
how_it_makes_money: Resale margin; some operators reportedly make $10K/month
startup_cost: low to medium: needs a van and storage
evidence: 'I know guys that are making 10 grand a month just flipping couches. If you live in a college town, you should be in the couch business' (IYotH4hI4KA)
risks: Physical and in-person work
Seasonal demand
Needs storage space

name: Simple cleaning service
one_liner: Start a cleaning business for homes, commercial spaces or exteriors with almost no capital.
evidence: 'Go clean something, man... you can make 50 bucks an hour doing it' (KSQF7cYG8gU)
Nick Huber: 'I got my first 7,000 customers without paying for any marketing' using chalk ads (KSQF7cYG8gU)
risks: In-person and labour-heavy
Async only once you have managers
Low barriers to entry
